claims.claim: Verizon's mobility-plus-broadband convergence links spectrum/5G and fiber infrastructure to household and enterprise connectivity needs; the Frontier acquisition materially expands the fiber side of that system and therefore the addressable convergence footprint.
The causal path is not dependent on equipment revenue: service growth, broadband additions and network reach are the more durable bridge from infrastructure to recurring connectivity demand.

causalEdges: spectrum+5G network -> mobile connectivity capacity -> consumer/enterprise communications need
fiber footprint -> fixed broadband capacity -> home/business connectivity need
fiber+mobile convergence -> bundled distribution/customer economics -> retention and recurring service demand
network capital+debt capacity -> infrastructure expansion -> future service reach

risks.risk: Cable, AT&T, T-Mobile, MVNOs and other fixed/wireless substitutes constrain pricing and make network quality plus convergence execution necessary rather than sufficient.

contradictions.contradiction: Lower equipment revenue can coexist with improving service economics; this weakens total-revenue optics but does not by itself falsify the service-network causal thesis.

unknowns.unknown: The durable incremental retention and ARPA benefit attributable specifically to Frontier-enabled convergence is not yet established.

claims.claim: Frontier strengthened Verizon's fiber reach but also raised financing exposure: Q1 2026 net unsecured debt was $130.1B and net unsecured debt/adjusted EBITDA was 2.6x after closing the acquisition.
Verizon has demonstrated active deleveraging through Frontier debt repayment and 2026 note redemptions, reducing but not eliminating balance-sheet sensitivity.

risks.risk: Large absolute debt makes the convergence strategy sensitive to integration execution, rates and sustained free-cash-flow delivery.
Intense telecom competition and promotional response can absorb network advantages into customer incentives rather than durable pricing power.
Network outages, cyber events and supplier disruptions are direct failure modes because reliability is itself part of the product.

contradictions.contradiction: Capital returns and network investment are being pursued alongside elevated post-acquisition debt; cash generation currently supports both, but deterioration would force a sharper allocation tradeoff.

unknowns.unknown: Full Frontier synergy realization and post-integration churn economics remain unproven over a complete operating cycle.
